definition: Myofascial pain syndrome is a common musculoskeletal pain condition involving sensitive trigger points in skeletal muscles and nearby tissues that can produce characteristic referred pain. It often includes regional pain, muscle spasm, reduced movement, and lower day-to-day functioning, and is seen more often in people exposed to repetitive strain, prolonged fixed posture, or work-related overuse.
